text: My husband I went here for breakfast and were excited to find a new breakfast treasure. We have wanted to come here for the past year, but for some reason or another we always forget this is an option. The views are amazing! You don't get tired of the ambiance. The food and coffee are good as well. My husband had the vanilla bean dipped french toast and I had the bacon & eggs. The bacon is thick and cooked perfectly. I can't wait to explore some of the other items on the menu.
Nothing like a hole in the wall that is hard to find...Unless you are a local and in the know. I haven't had a single item here that I did not thoroughly enjoy, Even their Chicken noodle soup!

Ok, so I'm at a conference above the Marketplace where this is located. This line for this place was significantly longer than the other stalls...and the people in the line seemed to be locals. What a treat!!! I did the roast beef with sharp provolone (such a better option than normal provolone) and mixed hot and sweet peppers. It was delicious...juicy but not greasy, flavorful, the peppers were fabulous. I should also mention that my server was as sweet as possible. Overall a great experience!
Over rated place. Had the short ribs and they tasted like pot roast. Not what I expected at all. Got dirty plates.
Very cool place! Perfect for a short walk at midnight from our rental. Would definitely come back for a burger/beer.

CASH ONLY! Ok now that that's out of the way, we came here over Mardi Gras weekend for lunch. The line was out the door! I thought this was just because of the heavy holiday weekend traffic but it looks like it's always like that from the pictures on their Yelp page. We waited in line, half way up it, people at the front of my group start yelling to the rest of us it's cash only. Do we all have enuogh cash? No. Some had no cash at all (me). So, we leave to go to an ATM, come back, start the line over again. My "po boy" is $13. Whatever. Food: I got the Shrimp Po boy and I will say they loaded up the shrimp, which was good. The bread was nothing special and the lettuce was like the shredded Subway stuff. Why on earth would anyone pay $13 for this? This place is just for tourists I think. I can't imagine why anyone who lived there would frequent this place. PS- this might just be me being a total "tourist" but isnt a "po boy" the same thing as a "sandwich" Lol?

Ye Olde College Inn has been around a very long time - and the quality of the food and scope of selection has never been better. The bar area is great with a Tulane and other local sports orientated theme. Attractive murals on the walls of the restaurant depict scenes from New Orleans circa the 1930's. Service is prompt, casual and friendly. If this restaurant were in any number of other cities, I would have given the food a strong 4 stars. However, given the standards of New Orleans, I decided to go with 3 on the food rating. However with the great atmosphere, quality of bar, friendly service and good food = 4 stars overall.

I'll start with the service which was horrible. It is a very small restaurant with waiters running around from left to right, yet we stood at the front for what seemed like 15 minutes before someone acknowledged us. There were plenty of open tables so we finally asked one of the staff if we could take a seat. Once we were seated we waited another 10-15 minutes before someone came to our table. Once we expressed our concern with the service they seemed to pick up their pace. Now onto the food. The menu is true Szechuan (pronounced Zesh-won) and has been rated one of the best in the country. After tasting it I am not surprised. What I loved most is that the menu is one page only not like other Chinese restaurants who present books as menus to flip through. There are your appetizers, entrees and side dishes. Szechuan is a style of Chinese cooking which originated from the Sichuan province of Southwestern China. What makes it so popular are the bold flavours, particularly the pungent and spiciness resulting from the use of mounds and mounds of garlic and chili peppers. You can choose your dishes based on the style of sauce you prefer and the meat or vegetables. Then you can choose the spiciness level ranging from 1 being tolerable to 10 being the spiciest. (See Menu) We started off with an order of wontons in chili oil. Once I took the first bite I was immediately hooked. I love garlic and am known to use a lot of it at home. What made the dish so special was the garlic chili sauce sprinkled with sesame oil. Next we tried the wontons in chili oil sauce. The flavors were the same although the wantons come in a larger quantity and seem to have more filling. It was also delicious. There were four of us on our second trip so we decided to order two main entrees and share. First order was the Dry Pot Style served in a mini wok and cooked in a spicy hot sauce with black mushrooms, bamboo shoots, bell peppers and Sichuan peppercorns. We ordered the level 7 spice thinking it was a happy medium. It arrived on top of a mini gas stove sizzling hot served with a big bowl of white rice. Again the sauce and the spiciness and the liberal use of garlic made it so good. In fact, the best I've ever had. We also ordered a side of bok choy with black mushrooms. It was presented so beautifully like a plate of flowers. It was the perfect side dish to offset the meat and spice. The bok choy was fresh and crunchy, the mushrooms were so good and the sauce even better. Our next entree was the prawns in garlic sauce. As if there was not enough garlic in the other dishes this plate was mainly covered in garlic. Did I complain? Of course not, it was truly one of the best sauces I have ever tasted. The prawns were large and generous amounts were presented in the plate. On our first trip we had the garlic sauce with the beef as opposed to the shrimp. I think I preferred the beef to the prawns for this dish. The garlic sauce is my favorite and I know that I'll be a regular based purely on this sauce. Just thinking of it is making my mouth water. Was the meal amazing? Yes. Will I be back? Yes. Did the service turn me off? A bit but the food is too good to let the bad service get in the way. Plus there are several different locations and I am determined to try them all.

I've gone here with several different people and no one is ever disappointed with the food!! Everything anyone has ever ordered has been delicious! I love the beer selection, it has the usual staples and seasonal changes. The service could sometimes be better, but it's what you'd expect from typical WC girls.

Steve's was my first cheesesteak after I moved to the area, and I have to be honest. I was fairly disappointed with my cheesesteak. I love that they have late night burgers, fries, and cheesesteaks. I got a classic cheesesteak with provolone and my steak was so dry! It was hard to take a bite without tearing the remaining steak out of the sandwich. The bread was nice and soft, the onions were perfectly caramelized, but the steak really dampened things. Their fries were good and I had a bite of my husbands burger (which was better than the cheesesteak). If you're not a fan of the shaved steak style of cheesesteaks, I would pass on Steve's.
My entree was dry, lacked flavor. My friend had the same and hers was equally as blah tasting. This was my first time going here, not sure I will go back.

The place is rather simple in its decor. The staff is rather average, but actually appropriate to the kind of place this is. The food tasted good, but then afterwards me and my friend didn't feel very good. I donno, it might have been a coincidence or maybe they fried the falafel in lard or other animal oil... We are both vegetarians and gluten free therefore we're definitely more sensitive to the quality of food.

Been to Panicos plenty of times, the staff is always friendly and prompt. They always have good drink specials and I am a huge fan of the pretzel bun burger. I love to stop in for a quick bite and a few beers. They have great selection of take out beer too.
Great place for lunch or dinner. Menu has an excellent selection of Italian dishes. Prices are reasonabe for wc and portions large. They offer a lunch buffet that you will love.

Food= five stars Guy behind counter on iPhone= 1 star Would love to leave five stars but the guy this morning of 11-30-21 at 11:45 was busy texting someone while I stood there. Back turned. No one but me in there so it's not like he didn't hear the door open. I said excuse me, he replied do you have a question. I replied I have a order. Maybe next time I'll luck out and get someone who wants to work and I'll give five stars. Kitchen staff was amazing too. Friendly and amazing food. Just one bad apple.

The atmosphere of this place is spot on, a renovated church that is open and beautifully lit. The bar is beautiful, complete with a sliding ladder! the dining room is cozy but not crowded, and the room sound is dialed in. The bartender was helpful and provided my friend a good option for her cocktail. He made her a special bourbon concoction and I ordered the green sizzle (omg, so refreshing!!!). We started with the pickle plate, it arrived quickly, was novel and fun, pickled strawberries anyone?! Plus kraut, carrots, and fennel. The pork belly app was the best I've had! The lamb burger was good but the French fries that came with were bomb and stole the show! Everyone at the table was eating them, soo good! A couple of us got the shrimp and grits, a little underwhelming - perhaps because everything else was so good. We will definitely return to try the other menu items!

We've been wanting to try August for YEARS and finally got there on Saturday night. The food varied but I was happy with what I had (we were a group of 4). The pasta dishes are on the high side but portions large. We were able to share the pasta with bolognese sauce for FOUR of us as an app. I had the spoecial crab cake ($23 I think) and it has no filler - but just one cake). The breadf pudding for dessert (I'm a big BP fan) ($7.00) was a bit too sweet. Service couldn't have been more inviting and it's a BYOB. It is CASH ONLY but that's not an issue. Parking can be because full neighborhood is 2 hour max (we were done in 1 3/4 hours. The main reason for 4 vs. 5 stars is the noise level. We were near the door (which is "quietest" place and at a square table for 4 we could hardly hear each other. And even though it was 55 degrees out the room was HOT with not much circulation. I'd recommend going but NOT on a weekend night - unless you want to YELL at each other.

We got here around 11:30 on a Sunday morning, which required about a 20 minute wait. That worked out for us because we learned it was BYO so quickly went to a wine store to get some champagne for our mimosas. Our order: the biscuits and gravy - it came with ham, sunny side egg with the biscuit and the gravy. The biscuit was ok - more cake like than biscuit. It was also a bit sweet. I wouldn't order this again. There are other places that have better (hungry pigeon or heritage) Lemon ricotta pancakes - this was great. Zesty lemon flavor and perfectly. The only complaint would be more sauce! My wife ordered the salmon pesto everything bagel that came with capers, and onions. She liked it! Pretty decent deal, esp when you factor the BYO.
3 stars is an optimistic assessment-cold food, wilted lettuce, tomatoe served looked like it was sliced yesterday..undercooked burger..
Nice gem of authentic food in south Philly. Restaurant is beautiful and the food is solid in flavor and portions.

I spent my birthday at Datz a few months ago. Not only were they really accommodating with our party (about 20 people or so) but the food was great and the service was even better. Next time you go, have The Kentucky Colonel Bowl! It was really good!

Ok... Just wanted to add that we are here on a Sunday afternoon to enjoy cold beers while poolside and in the pool. For a couple with no kids and who are used to "adult' poolside settings... This is NOT it. Kids running and screaming everywhere. More pool water in my cup than beer from the little turds doing cannonballs. Once we accepted this is not a sexy atmosphere, we have been enjoying the kid-insanity.
Great place for dinner and very enjoyable live band in the Gulch. Also cheap parking nearby

I'm a frequent doordasher in the carmel / westfield area. This fresh indian grill is never on time and it's always impossible to get help from the store employees. They get very backed up on the weekends and then you are stuck waiting for long amounts of time. I went here for lunch last week and waited 10 minutes in the lobby waiting to get my order taken. Pretty poor service

This place is consider new in town. The location is great with parking lots so u dont have to worry bout paying parking fee like in chinatown. The place is beautiful and it really great for party. I tried to have dinner with my husband and toddler son. It was Saturday night, but only me and another guess. I saw only 2 waitresses. The service was okay, I just dont agree that u clean the table while we're still sitting there. The menus are similar like u get in chinatown. We ordered dumplings, seafood and spinach soup, sweet and sour fish, crispy spicy beef. It tasted okay. Not so fabulous, but decent enough. I paid for 58 dolars. The price is higher than David's, but i like David's more. U can try to eat here if u need a beautiful place to eat. Or if u are too lazy to go to chinatown.

To start off, the service was prompt and thorough. Three types of water were offered. The water and the drinks were ordered. The drinks, bread and olive oil arrived. The game was afoot. Ordering was kinda hard. So many decisions to choose from. We settled on a three course meal with biscotti dessert. The food was impeccable. I had the best sword fish I've ever tasted. The pasta with pork black truffle sauce was on par with the pasta I sampled in Tuscany. The deconstructed biscotti was very cool. Fabulous. Hit up the very cool Passyunk neigherhood for one of the best Italian experiences I've had.

Great customer service at this one, the girl was courteous and kind and even delivered our food to us when it was ready. I like their fries better than Five Guys, but 5 Guys has them beat on the flavor. They do offer milkshakes which is also different. Seriously though you can't beat Charlies and its right down the street. This stop was all about convenience and location. I will never turn down a burger either!

We ended up at Fourth Street Shrimp Store after our first two choices were closed due to it being Monday night. This was our second visit. We had first tried Fourth Street Shrimp Store over 5 years ago. We couldn't remember if we liked it or why we never returned...now we know. Our meal can be summed up in two words: BLAND and OVERPRICED. I ordered the $14.99 blackened bay scallops. My Husband ordered the shrimp trio (which I believe was $18.99). We were both charged $1 extra because we didn't want coleslaw. When our food arrived I felt extremely underwhelmed. The plate looked like it came from a cafeteria. I still held out hope as I tried my first bites. I honestly ordered my scallops blackened because I thought it was "safe". Up until this point I have never had bland "blackened" food. The scallops were super tiny and lacking in flavor. Half of one sized was "blackened" with very little actual seasoning. I ordered the new potatoes and rice as my sides. The potatoes were decent tasting, but mainly because they tasted like they had been soaking in butter for hours. They still lacked seasoning. The rice was "meh". By the end of the meal I was drowning my plate in Crystal Hot Sauce, pepper, salt and the tarter sauce trying to make it taste good. It wasn't bad, it just wasn't good. My Husband's meal wasn't much better. The shrimp were small and bland. He liked the scampi shrimp the best, but once again...drowned in butter. That seems to be the only thing that this place knows to use to season food. He had the new potatoes and beans and rice as sides. He liked the beans at first and said they had a sweetness to them. However, a few bites in they were too monotone for him. Overall, we left still hungry, completely unsatisfied and $50 poorer. I will mention that we came shortly before closing and while they didn't say anything to us, we felt rushed. We only left a few minutes after they closed and the restaurant still had other patrons. So, it isn't like we were putting them out. We will not be returning. From other reviews I am guessing this place is best more for quantity on all-you-can-eat night. I don't recommend ordering here outside of that. Edible, but bland.

Its been awhile since I was last here which didn't leave a great impression on me because of poor service. I'm glad I came back. I would say service wasn't bad but more indifferent but that didn't really bother me since I really enjoyed the food. We ordered guacamole with an assortment of chips which I couldn't stop eating them! I then ordered the Raw Tuna Tostada which was SOO good. The dish came with 4 small tostadas topped with raw tuna so to some, this may not be considered enough for a meal but I found it enough, considering I ate a lot of chips with it. We got tres leches cake for dessert and wow. Definitely recommend. not too sweet. moist with warm sweetness. So delicious

White people's version of Asian food: a cross pollination of all Asian cuisine resulted in the most weird and unauthentic taste and overpriced. Some twists were interesting, although the noodle bowls tortured my Asian taste buds.
Everything has changed since Chef Ron signed on. Check out some of his gourmet additions. He is adding the "Gastro" to "Gastro-Pub." Keep up the good work, Chef

Twisted Waffles: So we made a resi because we had a table of 7. 4 adults and 3 kids, the place is not that large and they are social distancing. Our waitress was nice and very accommodating. We ordered the chicken and waffles, a sampler platter, shrimp and grits(not my fav), and some Cookie Monster waffles. Pros: besides the shrimp and grits( and it could just be my taste buds, because i didn't like the roux) the food was quite delicious. Seasoned to perfection, or just enough sweet. Wait staff was nice. Cons: the wait time for food. It was more than an hour before we got our food, from the time we ordered. Resi was at 1030, we didn't leave until almost 1 or later. The table next to us just left. We gave them a very extended time before we asked about it, once we asked about she said it was the next order up. Not sure if we should have asked sooner or it was just that slow. I also saw a lot of to go orders being serviced. (Not sure if this slows down the in costumer orders.) Overall I would try again. Because the food was really good. The potatoes and the chicken and waffles, but i would come with plenty of patient again.

Fine place and I'm happy to see a new restaurant open up in the neighborhood! Aside from the novelty of newness, I think nothing is really wrong with it, nothing is particularly right about it either. Has the feeling of a generic "nice" place you'd find in a cookie cutter type spot, like an airport or shopping mall. The interior presentation, the pricing, do not feel like a match to the neighborhood - for instance I paid nearly $50 for an appetizer and 6 tacos, which took 45 minute to prepare. Seems like an ambitious pricing model for what amounts to casual Mexican food in a very working class neighborhood. $4 per taco is steep no matter what's in it, no matter what part of town you're in. I think the food tastes very good but I doubt I would go back, there are better options at half the price with more personality within the vicinity.

I'm a huge fan of Sunday brunch, and I have discovered that Bixby's is a great place to go. They aren't the least expensive, but their selection of delicious brunch items is fantastic, and if you like a good breakfast cocktail, they make them perfectly! I'm a big fan of excellent service, and Bixby's never lets me down in that department, everyone is friendly and accommodating. Check this gem out!

Great Vietnamese food. Helpful waitresses, great service. I especially love their spring rolls-light and fresh with shrimp under the skins unless you ask for vegetarian. Food can be spicey. Great change on the usual Asian (Chinese) fare. Play with your palate! Mmm 12/15/11 update. We had another delicious meal, served promptly. Great spring rolls, made our ginger chicken entree hot to our liking. I'd rate the food 4 stars. HOWEVER. After-the-fact, when checking in on YELP, I am seriously concerned with the DIRTY DINING reviews--watched the TV reviews, went to the Health Dept report, saw that the same issues are occurring over a year now. I will not return to this restaurant until CLEAN reports are received. Roach infestations in the food prep area (live & dead) are too gross. These reports are severe violations, uncorrected with new ownership.

Small Italian grocery store that includes a menu of take out or eat in foods. Super casual, tables and chairs with the food served on disposable dishes... and we love it. We have tried deveral calzones, lasagna, and tirimasu. Ypu can call ahead and have dinner ready to take home. The lasagna will serve 2! We definitely recommend this spot!

We always eat in the bar as we love the bar server, Jose. Fantastic service! The wedge salad is the best we've evet had: freshest of lettuce, diced tomatoes; tasty lean bacon; ripe, sweet splinters of apples; great blue cheese dressing. Love the complimentary, warm loaf of bread. Jose puts garlic grains in a small dipping plate and pours herbed olive oil over it. Although it is no longer on the menu, Jose always talks the chef into making my favorite Carino original called Timballo. Spaghetti with sliced chicken, pepperoni, onions, mushrooms, green peppers, lots of melted mozzarella cheese on top, baked and served in a piping hot skillet. Not sure why they ever took this incredibly, delicious dish off the menu...just glad they'll still make it for me. Boyd tried an 8 oz steak, perfectly cooked to his desired medium rare and full of flavor. This is one of our very favorite restaurants in northern Nevada!

Yelp keeps removing my review, but I am describing an actual customer interaction. Green Eggs Cafe regularly allows it's waiting patrons to block the sidewalk, and that's not cool and that's not neighborly. And every time I have asked the host, hostess or manager to control their crowd i get some condesending bs answer along the lines of " you can just cross the street" or "there's nothing we can do" or "don't you have anything better to do?" It is a sidewalk, not your private waiting area, and I shall continue to barge my way thru and call you out on your boorish behavior, you arrogant, inept, unneighborly, sidewalk-blocking waffle-slapping bastards. Seriously, if Woody's can keep their sidewalk traversable, so can you. Green Eggs Cafe of 13th St--acn you please stop blocking the sidewalk?
Best burger I have had in a long time,A++on the service and a way to try different beer they brew will be back soon!

I don't know if I should give Eggshell Bistro a full review because I didn't actually get to eat here. But, I will post this so that hopefully Stephen owners will take some constructive criticism to make their business better. Style-wise this place had everything going for it to emulate a classic French bistro -- vintage decor, gypsy-swing music playing in the background, Wait staff dressed in gray denim shirts with newsboy caps, and a fantastic French-style menu (complete with quiche, tartes, and pastries. Loved the vibe they were going for. But, the service is where they definitely need improvement. When we arrived, the restaurant wasn't busy (though I did notice that quite a few tables had not yet been bussed and cleaned.) We had a group of three people in front of us, waiting to be seated. There didn't seem to be a designated host for starters, so none of the wait staff felt the need to approach any of us waiting at the door to seat us, presumably because they assumed any other of their counterparts were on top of it. So we waited at the door for probably about 10 minutes. After they finally acknowledged us and indicated a table for us to sit in, the server did not indicate if he would be taking care of us or if there would be another person assigned to our table. Another server presented us with a bottle of water and glasses, but didn't ask us for drinks or if we were ready to order. We waited for another 10-15 minutes for someone to help us, and by this time I was quite hungry and we had another place to be. So, we got up and left. I can tell this place has put thought behind their image, and I bet the food is good based on the Yelp pictures I've seen and other patrons' more positive experiences. Had we had more time, I would have been fine waiting. But, Eggshell Bistro's service was just too slow for us. I hope they take this constructive criticism to heart.

Have ordered Steffens Pizza before, but no specials. This time order dbl hamburger. Pizza came with dbl bacon. WHAT! Called the restaurant & spoke with mgr. "Oh yea, I remember that one. Probably just put dbl bacon on instead." Double WHAT. Ok, no trying to make it right? Nope. They do have great salads.
Olio was awesome! The decor, the staff, and food were great! I would highly recommend

Went in for brunch. Service was great but ordered the eggs Benedict and the poached eggs were hard boiled. The manager came out and assured us they would fix it. Their solution was undercooked eggs with watery egg whites. When we told the manager, he tried to convince us that eating raw eggs was safe!!??? After we expressed that we would not eat raw eggs, he told us to order something else because "they weren't going to get the eggs right." The bottomless mimosas were great but I would never go back. The food portions were small and the food was very below average. Would not recommend.

One of the best burgers I have ever had! In fact, I have had multiple different burgers from here and all would be on my top ten best burgers list! The atmosphere can be a little off, especially if you're not a big fan of Rock music, and it could be a bit cleaner, but in a way, those two things can also be a bit of the charm if you are into this type of atmosphere! No matter your preferences for the atmosphere, I would strongly encourage you to come in and try one of their amazing burgers!

Came here for dinner with my sister and friend on a sunday night. we got seated right away. The inside is very dark, it was kind of hard to see the menu. We ordered jambalaya, rice and beans with cajun fried chicken and my sister got a salad and asked for bread on the side. The food came very quickly within 10 minutes! The jambalaya was very salty! However, my sister never got her bread or the salad dressing! My friend's rice & beans and fried chicken was a good proportion. The jambalaya portion was very small for the price! Overall, it was OK. I dont think I would go back here again. There are better places to eat in NOLA.

The food was pleasantly delicious and very affordable. The atmosphere is unique and bold. I'd recommend this place to anyone. This is not your ordinary Mexican restaurant. I can't wait to go back and try more !

We stopped in a couple weeks ago and loved the build your own burger type deal they have going on. Fries were great which is imperative for a burger joint. Staff seemed excited to be there and were all polite and helpful! We will return!

My goodness where do I start? We went there with some friends and family to celebrate 2 Birthdays! We started with the table side guacamole, ribs, and chicken wings which were all amazing! 2 people had the Cowboy steak which was a great show of fire when they pours the conac sauce over the steak and hot plate. It was Great! I had the special which was Halibut over shrimp risotto (very good) someone had the trout and also said it was very good. Another had the beet salad and Crab cakes and also said it was good. My son had the spinach fettuccine dish with shrimp, scallops and crab he said it was very good too! Cocktails were amazing and the service was Amazing! And then came dessert OMG. I think we were all in a good coma! Thank goodness we ate early cuz we were so full I thought we were going to have to be rolled out LOL, we were first timers so we will definitely be going back. bTW where comfortable expandable pants!
Vegetables are from a can. Very similar to other chains, such as Pizza Hut. Overpriced.

Enjoyed a great meal, the live music was great and the speakers throughout the restaurant were mixed perfectly for sound. I sat at the bar and still felt like I had a great seat for live music, good drinks, and the food was fantastic.
